sections.summary: Sally Kornbluth is the President of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Kornbluth stated MIT already meets or exceeds many of the compact's proposed standards, citing MIT's reinstated SAT/ACT requirement (2022), international enrollment of about 10% of undergraduates, free tuition for incoming undergraduates from families earning under $200,000, and 94% of undergraduate degrees in STEM fields. Kornbluth underscored free expression as a core MIT value, writing: "We must hear facts and opinions we don't like — and engage respectfully with those with whom we disagree." Kornbluth authored a public letter to U.S. Education Secretary Linda McMahon explaining MIT's rejection of the compact.
